heading_ja: 文字間での分割の可否

cases.quote: Line break opportunities between two adjacent characters of given character classes explained in § 3.9.2 Grouping of Characters and Symbols depending on their Positioning shall be determined by Table 2.
cases.rationale: Table 2's own cell for an opening bracket (cl-01) followed by a middle dot (cl-05) carries no note of its own — no citation among §C.2's thirteen or §C.3's addendum — so the sentence a report names for it is this bare address, exactly as an unnoted Table 1 cell is answered by §B's own opening sentence and an unnoted Table 3 cell by §D.1's legend. The prohibition itself follows from cl-01's own row: an opening bracket never precedes a break against any trailing class Table 2 lists, kinsoku strictness notwithstanding, which is why one policy-free entry is every reading this case needs — §C.1's four kinsoku levels have nothing left to disagree about once the cell's own token is `not` rather than a level bitmask.

forbidden.why: Table 2's own cl-01 row prints `not` against every trailing class it lists, unconditioned on the kinsoku strictness §C.1 otherwise selects between; reading this coordinate as breakable at any level ignores the row's own marking rather than reading a level bit it does not carry.
